title: Preparation of Complaint Matrices for Quantifying Cellular Contraction
protocol: Place coverslips in a stainless steel holder rack.
Dilute full strength 3-aminopropyltrimethoxysilane in isopropanol for a final concentration of 2%.
Immerse coverslips in the silane-isopropanol solution for 10 min while gently stirring.
Wash coverslips by immersing in ddH2O (4 exchanges).
Soak coverslips in the final exchange of ddH2O for 10 min with stirring.
Dry coverslips in an incubator at ~37°C for 10 minutes.
Cool coverslips to room temperature.
Immerse coverslips in a 1% glutaraldehyde solution in ddH2O for 30 minutes.
Wash coverslips by exchanging with ddH2O (3 exchanges) for 10 min per exchange, stirring.
Dry coverslips at room temperature, covering with aluminum foil.
Prepare stock solutions of acrylamide/bis-acrylamide mix from 40% acrylamide and 2% bis-acrylamide.
Maintain stock solutions at 4°C in a darkened bottle for several years.
Obtain working solutions containing the final desired concentrations of acrylamide/bis-acrylamide from stock solutions.
Degas acrylamide solution in a vacuum chamber for 20 minutes.
Prepare 10% ammonium persulfate (APS) solution (0.5g/5mL).
Wipe a 1x3" microscope glass slide with Rain-X wipes vigorously to make the surface hydrophobic.
Remove excess Rain-X by wiping the glass slide with damp Kimwipes.
Set the glass slide aside, covered.
Remove acrylamide solution from vacuum chamber.
Add 5 μl of fluorescent beads (1% by volume) to the acrylamide solution.
Add 0.75 μl TEMED and 2.5 μl 10% APS to initiate gel polymerization.
Mix well by pipetting for approximately 5 seconds to minimize bubble introduction.
Apply 10-12 μl of the acrylamide solution to a hydrophobic microscope slide.
Place an activated 22x40mm coverslip on top of the droplet, ensuring that the gel solution coats the entire coverslip.
Smooth out any bubbles that may appear within the solution.
Allow the gel solution to polymerize at room temperature for approximately 10 minutes.
Assess completion of polymerization by inverting remaining working solution in a microcentrifuge tube and observing if the polymerized gel pulls away from the coverslip edges.
Immediately after macroscopic polymerization is observed, separate the coverslip from the glass slide using the fine tip of tweezers or a razor blade edge.
Carefully remove the coverslip with the attached gel and immerse it in ddH2O to maintain hydration.
Prepare 40 μl working aliquots of Sulfo-SANPAH by dissolving Sulfo-SANPAH powder in anhydrous dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO) (20 μl per mg of Sulfo-SANPAH).
Flash freeze stocks in liquid nitrogen and store at -80°C for later use.
Remove ddH2O from gel surface using a coverslip spinner (< 2sec).
Avoid drying the gel.
Dilute Sulfo-SANPAH-DMSO aliquots in ddH2O (2mg/ml, pH 7) immediately before use and coat gel surface (~200 μl).
Expose gel surface to UV light in a UV cross-linker oven (8W, 254 nm wavelength at a distance of 2-3 inches for 1.5 min).
Dip UV-treated coverslips in a beaker with fresh ddH2O.
Remove excess water from gel surface using a coverslip spinner.
Pipette ~50 μL of cold 1mg/ml Fibronectin (FN) in PBS, pH 7.4, on Parafilm in Petri dish container.
Invert coverslip on top of FN drop, gel side exposed to FN.
React at room temperature for 1-2 hours or at 5°C overnight.
Place coverslips in 6 cm tissue culture dishes containing PBS (pH 7.4) under sterile conditions in a tissue culture hood.
Wash extensively with several washes (3-5) of PBS (pH 7.4) under sterile conditions.
Sterilize the coverslips by use of germicidal lamp in tissue culture hood for 30 min.
Incubate coverslips in cell media for 30-45 min prior to plating cells.
Cross-link carbohydrate groups on proteins with hydrazine hydrate.
Prepare polyacrylamide gels as described in section 2.
Place PAA gel coverslips in plastic Petri dish in a fume hood and pipette approximately 1 ml of undiluted hydrazine hydrate onto the surface of each PAA gel.
Incubate for at least two hours, but no longer than 24 hours.
Add ddH2O to the Petri dish; remove hydrazine hydrate solution and dispose as hazardous waste.
Add 5% acetic acid to the Petri dish to immerse coverslip.
Cover and incubate for one hour.
Remove the acetic acid from coverslips.
Wash coverslips with ddH2O.
Incubate coverslips in ddH2O for one hour.
Dilute 10 μl of 1 mg/ml FN solution in 940 μl of 50 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH 4.5) to a final concentration of 10 μg/ml.
Make a stock of 20X sodium meta-periodate by adding 80 mg of sodium meta-periodate to 1 ml of 50 mM sodium acetate buffer (pH 4.5).
Add 50 μl of the 20X sodium meta-periodate stock to the FN solution, achieving a final concentration of 10 μg/ml FN and 4 μg/ml sodium meta-periodate.
Incubate the mixture in a dark tube at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Remove excess ddH2O from activated gel surface using a coverslip spinner (< 2 sec).
Pipette ~500 μl of the modified FN solution onto the activated gel surface and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.
Place coverslips in dishes containing PBS (pH 7.4) to cover them completely.
Wash coverslips extensively with several washes (3-5) of PBS (pH 7.4).
Sterilize coverslips using a germicidal lamp in the tissue culture hood for 30 minutes.
Incubate coverslips in cell media for 30-45 minutes before plating cells.
Conjugate ECM protein of choice to Acryloyl-X per manufacturer's instructions.
Store stock solutions of conjugated protein at 4°C.
Calculate volume of PAA working solution required for gel fabrication (e.g., 10 μL per coverslip).
Subtract 50 μL of water from the amount listed in the working solution recipe.
Initiate polymerization by removing calculated volume and adding ECM/Acryloyl-X solution to 10% volume (e.g., 1 μL of ECM/Acryloyl-X to 9 μL of PAA solution).
Perform step rapidly as gel is polymerizing.
Complete steps 2.6 and 2.7 as described previously.
Wash extensively with several washes (3-5) of PBS (pH 7.4), under sterile conditions.
Sterilize coverslips by use of germicidal lamp in tissue culture hood for 30 min.
Incubate coverslips in cell media for 30-45 min prior to plating cells.
Warm cell media and 0.5% or 0.25% trypsin.
Load warmed cell media and trypsin into a 5ml or 10ml syringe.
Load a 22x30mm coverslip onto the Top Coverslip holder of a Warner Instruments confocal imaging chamber (RC-30WA) using vacuum grease to keep the coverslip in place.
Place a chamber forming rubber gasket on top of the coverslip.
Load syringes onto inlet tubing via connector kit.
Check that media flows through tubing and onto Top Coverslip with no bubbles visible.
Apply vacuum grease onto base of chamber.
Load gel-coated 22x40mm coverslip, cell-side up, into the chamber base.
Place Top Coverslip holder onto chamber base with Chamber Gasket separating it from the gel-coated coverslip.
Ensure that Locating Pins within the chamber base sit within the Locating Holes in the Top Coverslip.
Apply the Pressure Plate to the chamber base and secure it using the Pressure Plate Wrench.
Check the flow of media through tubing and chamber for any leaks or media-free zones.
Eliminate media-free zones on the cell surface if necessary by drawing a slight vacuum while infusing with media.
Apply the confocal imaging chamber to the Stage Adapter situated within a microscope holder.
Image fluorescently-labeled protein and fluorescent beads embedded within the gel substrate using a confocal fluorescence microscope.
Perfuse trypsin to detach cellular adhesions from the gel.
Take an image of fluorescent beads in the same imaging field where the cell adhered.
Compare strained and unstrained bead positions for quantification of gel substrate displacement under contraction.
Activate coverslips by amino-silane/glutaraldehyde treatment.
Polymerize a polyacrylamide gel containing fluorescent beads onto the activated coverslip.
Chemically cross-link extracellular ligand to the surface of the polyacrylamide gel using one of the three coupling techniques listed in step 3.
Plate cells onto the gel and allow them to adhere and spread.
